fieldMarks: Male: black bib, white cheeks, gray crown and chestnut nape
Female: pale buff eyebrow, plain gray chest, black and buff stripes on a brown back
behavior: Forages mostly hopping on the ground; will perch on weed stalks for seeds and search car fronts and bark for insects
Mostly weed and grass seeds and waste grain, also insects in summer and human food scraps in cities
Shrill, monotonous, noisy chirping; permanent resident
habitat: Cities, towns and farms; in North America essentially always around manmade structures, never in unaltered natural habitats.
range: Native to the Old World; introduced and established from the north coast of British Columbia and southern Yukon to Newfoundland and south beyond North America.
